Subject: Follow-up: Observability & inference comparisons - next tests

Hi Sarah -

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Recap from today's discovery:
- ACME is evaluating inference providers for customer-facing assistants and product search. Key priorities: tail latency (p95/p99), predictable cost, and end-to-end observability (traces + per-request logs).
- Current shortlist: hyperscaler-managed endpoints (GCP/AWS), and a few inference APIs. You're most concerned about network egress unpredictability and the lack of consolidated tracing across app + inference.

What Redwood can provide / differentiators we highlighted:
- Unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you can prototype on hosted and then move to Dedicated or Private without code changes.
- Production-focused observability: per-route latency/cost breakdowns, token-level cost attribution, and request-level tracing that integrates with common APMs.
- Smart routing & fallbacks: automatic fallbacks to lower-cost variants or regional endpoints during capacity constraints.
- Cost controls: batching/quantization recommendations and cache-aware execution to reduce tokens and egress.

Suggested next tests (minimal POC):
1) Latency & tail behavior: run a 48-hour test against a customer-like query set; compare p50/p95/p99 and cold-starts vs your current hyperscaler baseline.
2) Observability integration: instrument the app to pass request_id and set up OpenTelemetry traces to confirm correlation between app-side traces and inference traces in Redwood Console + export to Datadog/Splunk.
3) Cost delta analysis: run identical workloads to measure cost per 1M tokens (hosted + edge egress) and quantify egress/egress mitigation options (regional routing, dedicated capacity).

Attachments: I attached a short comparison doc that outlines the hyperscaler tradeoffs we discussed and initial test plan.

Proposed timeline / next steps:
- If this looks good, we can kick off a scoped POC next week. Logan (cc'd) will share a test plan + infra checklist. David (cc'd) will follow up on pricing/contract for a short reserved window if you want Dedicated capacity for the POC.

Can you confirm: 1) sample dataset availability, and 2) a primary contact (Tom?) to help with infra access and firewall rules?

Thanks - talk soon.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Appreciate the recap and the doc - very helpful. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side before we lock in a POC: 

1) Egress & network costs: can you confirm how Redwood accounts for egress when running hosted inference vs Dedicated in our cloud region? Our finance team is sensitive to potential surprise egress fees.
2) Tracing: we use Datadog currently. Do you have examples of the trace export shape and how request_id correlation works in practice?
3) Integration effort: how much dev work should we budget to pass request_id and wire OpenTelemetry spans?

If you can answer the above and send a concrete test plan + infra checklist, we can confirm internal approvals. Tom will be the infra lead - I'll loop him into the POC kickoff.

Also: interested in trying a short A/B comparing Redwood hosted vs our current provider (same model family) for a 2k queries sample.

Best,

Marissa / team - taking this on. Draft POC plan below (high level). I'll attach a more formal POC-test-plan doc to share with Acme.

POC objectives:
- Validate tail latency (p50/p95/p99) and cold-start behavior for the target model family
- Confirm end-to-end trace correlation between Acme app traces and Redwood inference traces in Datadog
- Quantify cost delta (tokens + egress) between Redwood hosted and their current provider

Technical scope & steps:
1) Data / harness: Acme provides ~2k sample queries + expected traffic profile (burstiness). We'll run 2x 48-hour runs: one against their current provider baseline and one against Redwood hosted. Optionally run with a short Dedicated window if they want isolation.
2) Metrics captured: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), token counts, batching stats, KV cache hit rates, error rates, and total egress.
3) Observability: instrument app to forward request_id header. Redwood will export inference spans to Datadog; we will provide example OTLP/span definitions and a snippet for the app to add. We'll validate trace joins by searching for request_id across app spans & inference spans in Datadog.
4) Dashboards: we'll provision a shared read-only dashboard showing per-route latency, token costs, and trace links.
5) Deliverables: POC run results, cost comparison, dashboard snapshot, and short recommendations (quantization/batching settings).

Infra & timeline:
- Time to run setup: 3 business days (infra + instrumentation)
- Run time: 2 x 48-hour runs (baseline + Redwood)
- Total expected calendar time: ~2 weeks from kickoff (including procurement approvals)

Dependencies / asks from Acme:
- Share sample queries and a staging endpoint to route queries from Redwood test harness
- Confirm a point of contact for firewall/IP whitelisting (Tom)
- Provide a short Datadog API key & sample app trace to validate span joins (we'll provide instructions)

Attachments: POC-test-plan.md (stub) - will flesh into a doc for Acme.

I'll draft the external-facing plan and send to Marissa for review before we send to Sarah.

Logan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
